blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, automation and transformation are strategic choices, not technology programmes. The real question is never "what can we automate?" but "what kind of company do we want this automation to help us become?" Without that framing, automation simply speeds up whatever the company was already doing — including its mistakes.

Good senior leaders start with the business they are trying to build and work backwards. They identify the few processes that, if genuinely transformed, would change how the company competes. They protect those projects from political interference. And they accept, honestly, that many other processes should be left alone, even if someone somewhere thinks they ought to be "modernised".

Transformation that changes what the company can do is worth enormous effort. Transformation that merely moves old problems into new interfaces is worth almost nothing — and yet it consumes the same amount of time and money as the real thing.

items.q: According to the text, what is the real question senior leaders should ask?
options: What kind of company do we want this automation to help us become?
How quickly can we cut costs?
items.why: "The real question is never 'what can we automate?' but 'what kind of company do we want this automation to help us become?'"

items.q: What happens when automation is applied without the right framing?
options: It speeds up whatever the company was already doing, mistakes included
items.why: "automation simply speeds up whatever the company was already doing — including its mistakes."

items.q: How do good senior leaders decide what to transform?
options: They copy the modernisation plans of rivals
They automate every process they can
They start with the business they want to build and work backwards
They follow the loudest internal voices
items.why: "Good senior leaders start with the business they are trying to build and work backwards."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Political interference can damage transformation projects
The real value lies in changing what the company can do
Every process should be modernised as a matter of principle
Some processes are better left untouched
items.why: Inferência: o autor defende deixar muitos processos em paz — modernizar por modernizar é justamente o que ele critica.

items.q: The final paragraph suggests that a cosmetic transformation is dangerous mainly because…
options: it costs as much as real transformation but delivers almost nothing
it is easier to reverse than a real one
it is technically impossible to deliver
items.why: Inferência: "worth almost nothing — and yet it consumes the same amount of time and money as the real thing." O desperdício é o mesmo custo por quase zero de valor.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie contestando uma proposta de transformação em reunião. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Before we approve anything, I want to be honest about what this proposal actually does. As it stands, it takes a process that has been broken for years and wraps it in a very expensive new interface. The clicks will look modern. Nothing underneath will have changed.

I've read the business case twice, and nowhere does it say how the company competes differently afterwards. That silence is the whole problem. If we can't articulate what we become, we are not transforming anything — we're just paying to make the old mistakes faster.

So here's what I'm proposing instead. Take the same budget and put it behind two processes that could genuinely change our position with clients. Those two, we protect — no political horse-trading, no scope creep, no committee redesigning them every fortnight.

And the process on the table today? Leave it alone. I know that's unpopular, because someone senior has decided it must be modernised. But modernising it changes nothing except the login screen. I'd rather spend that money once, on something that moves us forward, than spread it thin on work that quietly fails.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie say the proposal actually does?
options: It cuts the transformation budget in half
It wraps a long-broken process in an expensive new interface
It rebuilds a broken process from the ground up
items.why: "it takes a process that has been broken for years and wraps it in a very expensive new interface."

items.q: Why does Sophie call the business case's silence "the whole problem"?
options: It never explains how the company competes differently afterwards
It fails to name the vendor
It doesn't list the project team
items.why: "nowhere does it say how the company competes differently afterwards. That silence is the whole problem."

items.q: What does Sophie propose doing with the budget instead?
options: Delaying all spending for a year
Splitting it across every department equally
Putting it behind two processes that could change the company's position with clients
items.why: "put it behind two processes that could genuinely change our position with clients."

items.q: When Sophie says "no scope creep, no committee redesigning them every fortnight", she implies that…
options: the two protected projects need to be shielded from interference to succeed
the budget should be reviewed monthly
the projects should stay secret from clients
committees should approve every change twice
items.why: Inferência: proteger significa blindar contra interferência política e mudanças constantes de escopo.

items.q: What is Sophie's attitude toward modernising the process on the table today?
options: Enthusiastic, because a senior leader backs it
Reluctantly opposed, because it would change nothing but the login screen
items.why: Inferência: ela reconhece que é impopular e que um sênior quer modernizar, mas argumenta que muda "nothing except the login screen".

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Automation is a strategic choice, not a technology programme." A strategic choice is…
options: a decision about which tools to buy
a deliberate decision that shapes how the company competes
a task delegated to the IT department
items.why: Strategic choice = escolha estratégica: decisão deliberada que molda como a empresa compete.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Without the right ___, automation just makes old mistakes happen faster."
items.why: Framing = enquadramento: a forma de formular o problema que dá sentido à automação.

items.q: "They protect the flagship projects from political interference." This refers to…
options: internal power struggles that distort or derail the work
items.why: Political interference = interferência política: disputas internas de poder que atrapalham o projeto.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "Many processes work well enough — the wise move is to ___ them ___."
items.why: Leave alone = deixar em paz: não mexer no que já funciona.

items.q: "A cosmetic project can consume as much budget as a real transformation." To consume here means to…
items.why: To consume = consumir: gastar/absorver os mesmos recursos de tempo e dinheiro.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre automação e transformação. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the transformation budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new platform to one region before the rest." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Sophie pushed back on the proposal." She…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "None of these cosmetic tweaks will move the needle on how we compete." This means they will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "The old plan drifted because no one followed through on it." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.
